title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.14): fix g ≥ 2 (or at least g ≥ 1) and a rigidifying structure on curves. M_g^G is the fibered category, over the moduli of curves M_g, of triples (X, P, ∇). Here X is a smooth proper curve, P is a P^1-bundle (a PGL(2)-torsor) on X, and ∇ is a flat (integrable) connection on P. The irreducibility condition is Aut(P,∇) = 1. Page 14 gives equivalent conditions: (a) Aut(P,∇)=1; (b) the algebraic group Aut(P,∇) ⊂ PGL(2) is 0-dimensional; (c) P is neither of 'G_m type' P(L⊕O) nor of 'G_a type' P(E) with E an extension of O by O. This page adds further equivalent conditions in cohomological terms. Let 𝔤 = ad P, a rank-3 vector bundle with induced flat connection, and let H^i_DR(X,𝔤) be the hypercohomology of 𝔤 ⊗ Ω^•_X.

(d) dim H^1_DR(X,𝔤) = 6g−6.
(d') H^0_DR(X,𝔤) = 0.
(d'') H^2_DR(X,𝔤) = 0.

The argument has four steps.
(1) The Killing form gives 𝔤 ≅ 𝔤^∨ as flat bundles. De Rham Poincaré duality on a proper curve then gives (*) H^0_DR(X,𝔤) ≅ H^2_DR(X,𝔤)^∨, so (d') ⇔ (d'').
(2) Euler–Poincaré: χ_DR(X,𝔤) = rk 𝔤 · χ_DR(X,O_X) = 3(2−2g) = 6−6g. Algebraically this is χ(ad P) − χ(ad P⊗Ω) = 3(1−g) − 3(g−1), since deg ad P = 0. Combined with (*) this gives (***) dim H^1 = 2 dim H^0 + 6g−6, hence (d) ⇔ (d').
(3) H^0_DR(X,𝔤), the horizontal sections of ad P, equals Lie Aut(P,∇). Hence (d') ⇔ (b), and intrinsically dim H^1_DR = 2(dim Aut(P,∇) + 3g−3).
(4) H^1_DR(X,𝔤) is the tangent space to the fibre of M_g^G over the point [X] (first-order deformations of (P,∇) with X fixed). H^0 = infinitesimal automorphisms and H^2 = obstructions.

The concluding NB draws the consequences. At irreducible points M_g^G has neither infinitesimal nor finite automorphisms, so it should be 'rigid' (a sheaf rather than a stack), like a rigidified M_g. It is formally smooth over M_g because H^2 = 0, with relative dimension 6g−6 (total dimension 9g−9). Grothendieck conjectures relative representability, perhaps as an Artin algebraic space. The next page compares this, over C, with the character variety Hom^!(π_1, PGL_2)/PGL_2 via Riemann–Hilbert, which he notes is presumably not algebraic. The overall purpose is the 'projective connections and uniformization' project. The uniformizing (Fuchsian) projective connection gives a canonical, non-algebraic section of M_g^G → M_g, and one wants to understand the space in which it lives.
errors: A crossed-out line writes '6g−6−6g'. The correct value is χ_DR = 3(2−2g) = 6−6g, and Grothendieck uses the correct sign in (***).

The underbrace calls H^1_DR(X,𝔤) the tangent space to M_g^G. Strictly it is the relative tangent space over M_g, of dimension 6g−6. The total tangent space has dimension 9g−9, as the final NB about relative dimension makes clear.
The duality 𝔤 ≅ 𝔤^∨ via the Killing form needs 2 invertible. Over an arbitrary base, as on p.14, characteristic 2 must be excluded or handled with the trace form on End_0.

The remark on g: for g=0 the conditions never hold, since π_1 = 1. For g=1 they can hold, with 6g−6 = 0: an image Klein four-group in PGL_2 has finite centralizer, giving rigid isolated points, though not with Aut(P,∇) = 1. So the expected dimension is only meaningful for g ≥ 2. The margin remark is partly illegible.
Equivalence (d) ⇔ (b) needs Aut to be smooth, or dim Lie = dim Aut. This holds in characteristic 0 (Cartier) but needs care in characteristic p; Grothendieck states the condition as d') ⇔ b).

ideas.what: Deformation theory of flat PGL2-bundles via de Rham cohomology of the adjoint flat bundle: H^0 = infinitesimal automorphisms, H^1 = tangent space, H^2 = obstructions
ideas.modern_name: Deformation complex of flat connections / local systems (ad-valued de Rham complex)
ideas.where_published: General deformation formalism in SGA1/FGA style; not this specific application as far as I know

ideas.what: Killing-form self-duality plus Poincaré duality gives H^0 ≅ (H^2)^∨, and the Euler characteristic gives dim H^1 = 2 dim H^0 + 6g−6
ideas.modern_name: Dimension of the character variety / de Rham moduli space at irreducible points: (2g−2) dim G
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goldman (1984, symplectic nature of π_1 of surfaces)

ideas.what: Irreducibility (trivial automorphism group) is equivalent to vanishing of H^0, hence H^2, hence smoothness of dimension 6g−6
ideas.modern_name: Smoothness of the good/irreducible locus of the de Rham moduli space M_dR(X, PGL_2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goldman; Simpson (Moduli of representations I, II, 1994)

ideas.what: Relative moduli M_g^G over M_g of curves with an irreducible flat P^1-bundle: rigid, formally smooth of relative dimension 6g−6, conjecturally a relative algebraic space
ideas.modern_name: Relative de Rham moduli space over M_g (total dimension 9g−9), containing the space of projective structures/opers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Simpson (relative M_dR over a base S, 1994)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, purely algebraically and over a general base, the relative moduli of irreducible flat PGL2-bundles over M_g (total dimension 9g−9). He computes its deformation theory and conjectures relative representability as an algebraic space. This anticipates Simpson's relative de Rham moduli, but it is a standard computation, and the result is now well established.
missed.quote: La condition d'') implique que M^G_g est formellement lisse sur M_g, et d) que sa dim relative sur M_g est 6g-6. Sans doute peut-on prouver la représentabilité relative
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest only; the content is now standard (Goldman, Simpson). Its value is in documenting Grothendieck's algebraic framing of uniformization through moduli of flat projective connections.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a correct, standard deformation-theoretic dimension count for irreducible flat PGL2-bundles on curves, with a conjecture on relative representability. This is all now classical (Goldman, Goldman–Millson, Simpson). The undated manuscript may predate some of it, but nothing here would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: '= [-6g-6-6g-]' is a struck-out arithmetic slip; the intended value is 6−6g.
'3 χ^G(X,O_X)' is likely '3 χ_DR(X,O_X)', with the annotations 'rg 𝔤' under the 3 and '2−2g' under χ.
'tout comme M_g - dans un espace représentable !' is uncertain; it may read 'dans le cas rigidifié' or similar, given p.14's rigidifying functor.
'(conditions jamais vérifiée si g=0 - et vrai sauf !)' is uncertain; it plausibly reads 'conditions jamais vérifiées si g=0 – et g=1 ?' or 'et vrai cas !'.
The underbrace under H^1_DR reads approximately 'espace tangent à l'espace modulaire M^G_g aux pts correspondants à (X,P,∇)'.
